author: LeAnne Marie McPherson
title: Inspectors set to monitor food safety at local county fair; free resources available - NewsBreak
text:
By LeAnne Marie McPherson ,
6 hours ago
DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – The Darke County General Health District has shared some health advice for people and their kids planning to attend the Great Darke County Fair.
“The Health District urges everyone to stay hydrated, wear sunscreen and bug spray, and take breaks in designated rest areas, some of which are air-conditioned,” wrote the health district. “Visitors are encouraged to wash hands frequently after visiting animal barns and to avoid eating or drinking in those areas. Hand sanitizing stations are available at barn entrances and exits.”
The district is busy preparing for food safety inspections, and its inspectors will be on-site during multiple days of the fair to review the concessions.
SNAP recipients can use benefits to support many local farmers’ markets The rules for temporary and mobile food vendors include the following:
Using water from approved sources Disposing wastewater in approved drains or containers Having handwashing, hot water and dish sanitation spaces Obtaining food from licensed sources / preparing it safely For those camping, it’s important to remember to dispose of gray water in blue belly containers / holding tanks / sanitary sewers and to only use approved dump stations for black water .
There will also be free mosquito control resources (while supplies last) at the Darke County General Health District booth near the Grandstands.
For more information on the Darke County General Health District, call 937-548-4196.
